I am seventy-two years old and have farmed my six mu of flat land in Quzhou County for over fifty years. My legs are not what they used to be, so I do not take risks on new crops or labor-intensive ventures like cotton or vegetables. I stick with the wheat-maize rotation that my neighbors and I have grown all our lives. It is now spring, and the winter wheat I sowed last October is greening up. I will manage it through to harvest in early June, then immediately plant summer maize.

For my wheat, I use an improved variety—luyuan502, which I have grown for many years and know well. I will rotary-till the field before sowing. I apply compound fertilizer as basal dressing and then topdress with urea at the green-up stage. The wheat needs three irrigations: one at green-up, one at jointing, and one at grain filling. I spray insecticide twice for aphids, herbicide once for weeds, and fungicide once to prevent powdery mildew. I expect about 1000 jin per mu.

For the summer maize, I plant denghai605 hybrid seeds right after the wheat harvest, using no-tillage direct seeding—this saves time and labor, and the seed dealer guarantees good germination. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat: basal compound fertilizer is enough, with a small side-dressing at the jointing stage if rain is scarce. I irrigate twice, spray insecticide twice for corn borer, and apply herbicide once. I expect about 1100 jin per mu.
